replacements.value: Protective divine wrath can be compatible with love when it proportionately opposes genuine harm, imposes just accountability, and leaves wrongdoers a meaningful path toward forgiveness and restoration.

Knechtle could compare how probable each historical, moral, and experiential observation would be under Christianity and specific naturalistic alternatives, rather than merely listing considerations. The comparison should separate independent evidence from repeated reports of the same source, state contested premises openly, and weight each strand according to its provenance and reliability. He could then ask whether their combined likelihood ratio favors resurrection and theism, while testing sensitivity to disputed assumptions and conceding that modest cumulative support does not make any single observation demonstrative of a miracle.
